subject: Clarifying AI use rights, no-training evidence, and export workflow
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightwellhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Ian Murray <ian.murray@brightwellhealth.com>, privacy@brightwellhealth.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood: clarification on AI "no-training" promise + transfer path

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. A couple items popped up from our legal/privacy team as we move into procurement:

1) We need a written no-training commitment for Brightwell customer data — specifically, that Redwood will not use any customer inputs or outputs to improve or fine-tune models used to serve Brightwell. Is there a standard clause or addendum you provide?

2) Assuming a no-train commitment, what evidence or artifacts can Redwood provide on request (e.g., subprocessor list, audit logs, exportable prompt/response bundles)? Our auditors will want to see procedural proof, not just a contract promise.

3) We host certain PHI-adjacent logs on our SFTP. If we elect to require EU residency for derivative artifacts, can Redwood deliver a periodic export to our SFTP endpoint and certify the transfer path? If so, what format and cadence is supported?

We attached our security questionnaire and marked the sections that are blockers for us. Can you loop in legal/ops folks who can confirm what evidence and operational commitments Redwood is prepared to put in the DPA?

Appreciate a quick note on next steps — Ellen

--
Ellen Park
Head of Security & Privacy
Brightwell Health
ellen.park@brightwellhealth.com

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 18:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood: clarification on AI "no-training" promise + transfer path

Ellen — thanks for the clear list and for sending the questionnaire. Looping in Monica (Customer Success / Ops) and Connor (Security/Compliance liaison) so we can respond with specifics and evidence artifacts.

Quick answers up front:
- We can commit to a no-training clause for your account (Brightwell) and include it in the DPA/addendum.
- We have an evidence pack we provide for customers asking for operational proof: subprocessor inventory, per-route request logs (redacted to meet privacy demands), and an artifacts export (zipped JSON/CSV of prompt/response bundles) under an agreed scope.
- SFTP exports are supported on a periodic basis; Monica will outline formats/cadence and the onboarding checklist.

Connor — can you confirm what our standard evidence pack contains vs. what would be added for PHI-adjacent customers requesting EU residency of artifacts? Also, any comments on the draft no-train wording if legal wants to redline?

Happy to set up a short call tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightwellhealth.com>, Ian Murray <ian.murray@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Redwood: clarification on AI "no-training" promise + transfer path

Forwarding internal summary and proposed evidence package for Ellen's review. See below and attached drafts.

Internal notes (for the thread):
- Evidence pack (standard) includes: subprocessor inventory (latest snapshot), system architecture diagram, per-route redacted logs for a rolling 30-day window, MD5 manifest of artifacts exports, and the security questionnaire responses.
- No-train commit: we propose a DPA addendum that states "Redwood will not use Customer-provided content (inputs or outputs) from the Brightwell account to train, fine-tune, or improve models used in production for other customers, except with explicit written consent." We also add an operations paragraph describing access controls and tokenization/segregation safeguards.
- EU residency/export: we can offer scheduled SFTP exports (encrypted tar.gz) delivered monthly or on-demand. Format: CSV (metadata) + NDJSON (prompt/response bundles) with a signed delivery manifest. For High-Sensitivity accounts we can set retention and disable long-term logs.

Attachments included in this email to customer: no-train-commitment-draft.docx (proposed DPA language), Brightwell_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (completed responses), sftp-specs.csv (export field mapping).

Monica — can you craft a short customer-facing email that summarizes commitments and the next steps for SFTP onboarding? If Brightwell needs a shorter SLA for delivery cadence we should capture that as a follow-up item.

Connor
Security Engineering (Compliance Liaison)

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightwellhealth.com>, Ian Murray <ian.murray@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood: clarification on AI "no-training" promise + transfer path

Hi Ellen — thanks for the questionnaire. Attaching the evidence pack and a proposed DPA addendum for your legal team to review (docs attached in the forwarded message). Summary of what's included and immediate next steps: 

What Redwood will commit to (high level):
- No-training: Redwood will not use Brightwell inputs/outputs to train or improve models serving non-Brightwell customers without explicit written consent. The addendum includes operational controls and a 30/90 day window for retention options.
- Evidence: subprocessor list, architecture diagram, sample redacted logs, and an artifacts export (NDJSON + CSV manifest). We also provide a signed MD5 manifest and a custodian contact for any transfer certification.
- Export & delivery: We support monthly automated SFTP exports to your endpoint (encrypted AES-256, signed manifest). On-demand exports can be requested with a 5-business-day SLA for non-sensitive scopes; expedited delivery is available via our enterprise support tier.

Action items for Brightwell:
1) Confirm whether you want monthly automated exports or on-demand only.
2) Provide SFTP endpoint + preferred username/key type, and whether you require EU residency for the artifacts.
3) Share any redlines to the attached no-train addendum; our legal team (Priyom cc'd) will review.

If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call later today to walk through the addendum and the onboarding checklist.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
snippet: No-train commitment, evidence pack, and SFTP export options — Monica to confirm cadence and legal review.
